Answers clips [{clip, media, state, progress, quality, frames, covered, ready, subject_found, centroid, error?}]: state is analyzing, ready (every frame analysed and a person, or a picture's foreground subject, found), no_person (every frame analysed and no person in the clip's window: the clip draws whole), no_subject (a picture with subject foreground whose mask found no subject: it draws whole), failed or no_picture (the clip plays no frame of its file); progress 0–1; quality the clip's; frames the frames of its file the clip plays (1 for a picture) and covered how many are analysed; ready whether covered equals frames; subject_found whether a subject was found; centroid {x, y}, the subject's mean centre over those frames in the media's upright pixels (origin top left, y down), null unless ready; error, when failed, the sentence saying why. Refused, nothing done: wait outs
89	  - wait : How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, 0 to 60; 0 (answer now) when left out. [number] 
90	  - clips : The cut-out clips to answer for; every cut-out clip in the open scope, in timeline order, when left out. [array] 
91	===== detach_audio
92	Splits a clip's audio onto its own clip on the track below (inserting one when there is none), muting the original's audio and hiding the new clip's video — ⌥⌘D. The two are LINKED (`linked` names the other): moves, splits, ripples, nests and copies keep them in step in time; trim_start or trim_end with alone: true on the sound makes a J- or L-cut; speed and reverse are refused until attach_audio. Refused, saying why, for a non-media clip, media with no audio, or audio already detached.
93	  - clip : Clip id (get_project lists them). [integer] 
94	===== attach_audio
95	Merges a detach_audio pair back into one clip — Clip ▸ Attach Audio (⇧⌥⌘D). Name either half. The picture's audio comes back on with the sound's audio settings and the sound clip goes. Refused when the clip is not linked, and when the two no longer cover the same time (a J- or L-cut): trim them to match first.
96	  - clip : Clip id (get_project lists them). [integer] 
97	===== ripple_delete_ranges
98	Cuts SEVERAL time ranges out of the whole timeline as ONE edit — what Clip ▸ Remove Silences… sends. Each pair is put in order (a reversed pair is the same range), the pairs are then MERGED — overlapping and touching alike — and the survivors are cut right to left exactly as ripple_delete_range cuts one. So this is NOT the same as calling that once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two. It is one undo step however many ranges there are, which is the point. Markers do not move, as under every ripple. An empty list, and a list that merges to nothing, change nothing. detect_silence returns ranges in this shape.
99	  - ranges : The spans to cut, each a [from, to] pair in TICKS — 600000 per second, so 1 s = 600000 and one 30 fps frame = 20000. Rounded to the project's frame grid. [array] 
100	===== detect_silence
101	Finds the quiet stretches of the timeline and REPORTS them, changing nothing — the read half of Clip ▸ Remove Silences…, whose Remove button sends the answer to ripple_delete_ranges. In voice mode (the default) a moment is quiet when the cached Silero VAD probability over it is under voice_confidence; a clip whose source window holds no voice anywhere, and every file when the model cannot be used, is judged by level — each 10 ms of the cached waveform times the audio envelope against threshold_db. In either mode a moment whose envelope alone puts full scale at or under threshold_db is quiet, so volume, fades, ducking, mute and another track's solo all count. A run quieter than threshold_db and at least min_length long is a candidate; it then loses padding at each end, and its bounds snap INWARD to the frame grid — which can leave a frame of room tone, where outward would clip the attack of the next word. A moment no clip in scope covers is not a candidate at all: a hole in the timeline is not dead air. The result reports the scope and mode it used, and names any media whose analysis is still running rather than counting it silent — the waveform, or in voice mode the speech. judged_by_level_clips names each clip judged by level, and proposed_by_mix_clips each clip a range is proposed inside only because the mix turns it down while its analysis is still running. A nest clip is a wall: no candidate reaches into one, and protected_nests names each nest clip a quiet run of at least min_length crossed — set_scope into it and call again to look for any dead air inside.
102	  - clips : Analyse only these clips — the sheet's Selected clips scope. Omit to take the sheet's own opening rule: the project's current selection when it holds anything with sound, every audible clip otherwise. The result says which ran. [array] 
103	  - padding : Left at each end of every candidate, in TICKS — 600000 per second, so 1 s = 600000 and one 30 fps frame = 20000. Rounded to the project's frame grid. Default 0.1 s (60000). From 0 to 9000000000000000. [integer] 
104	  - threshold_db : Quieter than this counts as silence, in dBFS in the mix. Default -40. [number] 
105	  - voice_confidence : In voice mode, the Silero probability at or above which a moment counts as speech. Default 0.5. Refused outside voice mode. [number] 
106	  - mode : voice (the default) judges by the cached Silero VAD probability, falling back to level over any clip whose own source window holds no voice; level is today's rule alone. voice is refused when the voice model could not be used this process — the result names it and omitting mode falls back to level w [string] ['voice', 'level']
107	  - min_length : The shortest quiet run worth cutting, in TICKS — 600000 per second, so 1 s = 600000 and one 30 fps frame = 20000. Rounded to the project's frame grid. Default 0.5 s (300000). From 0 to 9000000000000000. [integer] 
108	===== undo
109	Undoes one step — Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z). Every tool that edits the project makes exactly one step, so one undo walks back exactly one call. Reports the name of the step it undid. View-state tools (set_playhead, set_range) make no step. Errors when there is nothing to undo.
110	===== redo
111	Redoes one undone step — Edit ▸ Redo (⇧⌘Z). Any new edit clears the redo stack, exactly as in the app.
112	===== set_media_cursor
113	Attaches, moves or removes a screen recording's cursor file — the .fjcursor Frame Job writes beside each recorded movie, from which it draws the pointer, its clicks and its path — the Media tab's Cursor section ▸ Locate… (undo "Locate Cursor File") and Remove ("Remove Cursor File"). cursor is {path, bookmark?, in_picture}, the media's cursor as get_project shows it, or null to forget the file (the file itself is kept). The file is checked as Locate… checks it: it must open as a cursor file, its movie_size must be the movie's width × height, and in_picture must be the file's own (true when the movie's picture already shows the pointer), each refused in its own sentence. Refused too: an empty path, and a media that is not a video with a picture. Consolidate Media copies the file into the package beside its movie, and opening a moved package finds it there.
114	  - cursor : {path, bookmark?, in_picture}, or null to remove it. [object] 
115	  - media : The video media's id. [integer] 
116	===== get_cursor_events
117	Answers what a screen recording's cursor file holds — its clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, typing stretches and, asked for, its path — read ON THIS MAC from the media's .fjcursor (get_project's media[].cursor). With media, times are the file's own SOURCE ticks (time "media"); with clip, they are ticks from the clip's start (time "clip", through its speed and ramp), and each click and scroll also has q [qx, qy]: its position in the clip's region frame — an offset in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, the frame add_zoom_action's region takes, so a region around a click is {x: qx, y: qy, w, h}. x and y are the movie's own pixels from its top-left; size is [w, h]. clicks [{t, button (0 left, 1 right, 2 other), down (1 press, 0 release), count, x, y, q?}], scrolls [{t, x, y, dx, dy (points), q?}] (each a single wheel event), shortcuts [{t, keys, code}], typing [{from, to, marks}] (stretches of typing, each overlapping the window), path {smoothing, t, x, y} sampled 10 times a second at the clip's smoothing (0 for media) unless smoothing is given. Rows of every kind and path samples count together: an answer holds at most 5000, and next is then the first time left out — call again with from: next. A clip that plays reversed is refused (ask with its media), as is a media with no cursor file or one whose file is missing. It edits nothing and makes no undo step.
118	  - clip : A media clip of a recording: its events in clip time, with q — exactly one of media and clip. [integer] 
119	  - to : Where to stop (not included), in TICKS — 600000 per second: the media's or the clip's duration by default; must be after from. [integer] 
120	  - kinds : Which to answer: clicks, scrolls, shortcuts and typing by default; add path for the pointer's path. [array] 
121	  - from : Where to start, in TICKS — 600000 per second, in the answer's time: 0 by default. [integer] 
122	  - media : The recording whose events to read, in its own source ticks — exactly one of media and clip. [integer] 
123	  - smoothing : The path's smoothing, 0–1 (path only): the clip's own Cursor ▸ Smoothing by default, else 0, the raw path. [number] 
124	===== get_media_analysis
125	Answers an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays, made ON THIS MAC — no network request, no upload, no API key — and kept per media in the project's cache, so a later call over a window already analysed answers at once. kind "shots" finds the hard cuts: cuts is [{frame, source}] sorted by time, frame the media's frame index and source its presentation time in the media's own SOURCE ticks (600000 per second, of the file played forwards), with count. A cut inside a gradual dissolve is not reported, and a single flash frame is not a cut; a dissolve between flat-coloured pictures (slides, title cards) can show as one cut. kind "masks" finds a person's outline in every frame (Vision's person segmentation, on the Mac) and answers its runs, never pixels: mask_size [w, h] (the masks' own size), frames (frames held in the window), subject_found (whether any frame holds a person: at least 0.5 % of the mask above half), count and runs [{from, to, subject_found, frames}] in SOURCE ticks — a run is consecutive analysed frames that agree on subject_found. Remove Background (Clip ▸ Remove Background, the Clip tab's Picture ▸ Background section, set_video cutout) draws them, and analyze_cutout makes a cut-out clip's masks and says where they stand. kind "faces" finds every face (Vision's face rectangles and landmarks, on the Mac) at 10 samples a second of source time and answers rate, count and samples [{source, frame, faces: [{box: [x, y, w, h], confidence, roll, yaw, mouth_gap, mouth_width}]}]: source the sample's instant in SOURCE ticks, frame the presentation time of the frame it read (the first at or after source, within one sample) or null; box 0…1 of the upright picture from its top-left; roll and yaw in radians; mouth_gap the inner lips' height and mou
126	  - media : The media whose picture or sound to analyse — exactly one of media and clip. [integer] 
127	  - kind : What to find: shots, the hard cuts; masks, a person's masks' runs; faces, every face per sample (box, roll, yaw, mouth); sound_events, laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech per window of sound; subjects, people and salient regions per sample. [string] ['shots', 'masks', 'faces', 'sound_events', 'subjects']
128	  - from : Where to start, in the media's SOURCE ticks (the file played forwards, 600000 per second), not snapped: 0, or the clip's played window's start, by default. [integer] 
129	  - to : Where to stop (not included), in the media's SOURCE ticks: the media's end, or the clip's played window's end, by default; must be after from. [integer] 
130	  - clip : A media clip: its media analysed over the part the clip plays — exactly one of media and clip. [integer] 
131	===== set_media_color
132	Sets how a video file's camera log footage is converted to Rec. 709 — the Media tab's Camera Log popup. Every clip of the file, and its reverse, follows it; it is converted before the chroma key and every grade, and Show Ungraded keeps it. color is {log, gamut?}: log apple_log (gamut bt2020), apple_log2 (apple_wide_gamut), slog3 (s_gamut3_cine or s_gamut3), vlog (v_gamut), canon_log2 or canon_log3 (Canon Log 2 and 3: cinema_gamut or bt2020), gamut defaulting to the first; or {lut: media id} to convert with an imported .cube (import_media it first); or null for none, which shows the log picture. An Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is set at import (get_project's media[].color shows detected: true). Camera Log is refused on an audio, image or LUT media. A PQ (HDR10) file — a video, or a PQ still image — also takes peak, a whole number of cd/m² 1–10000 — the Media tab's HDR10 Peak field: where its highlights roll off to white. Import reads the file's own peak into media[].color.pq {file, from} (MaxCLL, else the mastering display's maximum; {} when the file names none, which means 1,000), and peak overrides it. color replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so send both to keep both; null clears both and keeps the file's reading. A PQ still takes {peak} alone. A peak on a file that is not PQ is refused.
133	  - color : {log, gamut?}, {lut} or {peak}, log or lut beside peak, or null to clear. [object] 
134	  - media : The video media's id, or a PQ still's for peak alone. [integer] 
135	===== add_shortcut_overlays
136	Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip per keyboard shortcut recorded in screen recordings' cursor files, at the moment it was pressed, as ONE undo step "Add Shortcut Overlays" — Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays. Only shortcuts are recorded (Record shortcuts in the recorder), never typed keys. Each press inside a clip's played window is placed through the clip's speed and ramps, snapped to the frame grid. An overlay lasts duration seconds and never less than (10 × keycaps + 25) frames, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it to duration after the last press, labelled ×2, ×3 … (merged counts them); a different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, waiting until the earlier one has had its minimum — and if that is more than 0.5 s after its press it is dropped (dropped counts them). Overlays never overlap. They go on the front-most track named "Shortcuts" when it is in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span; otherwise on a new "Shortcuts" track at the front (new_track). The project's graphics/ module whose text equals the bundled keyboard-keys template is reused; otherwise the template is copied in once (written), and only when something is placed. Refused: a clip that is not a media clip, whose media has no cursor file or whose file is missing, or that plays reversed. Answers added, dropped, merged, track, new_track, module, written and overlays [{at, duration, keys, label}] (at in container ticks); with no shortcut in the clips' played windows, ok with a note and no undo step.
137	  - clips : Media clips whose media have cursor files — exactly one of clip and clips. [array] 
138	  - clip : A screen recording's media clip — exactly one of clip and clips. [integer] 
139	  - duration : How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5–10, 1.5 by default (never less than the template's minimum). [number] 
140	  - theme : The keycaps' look: dark (the default) or light. [string] ['dark', 'light']
141	  - position : Where the keycaps sit: bottom (the default), center or top. [string] ['bottom', 'center', 'top']
142	  - from : Place only shortcuts at or after this container time, in TICKS — 600000 per second. [integer] 
143	  - to : Place only shortcuts before this container time, in TICKS — 600000 per second; must be after from. [integer] 
144	===== relay_captions
145	Re-lays the word captions for the current canvas — what File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas does — after set_canvas, or for captions laid on another canvas. It acts in the container set_scope has open (the timeline, or the open nest at the nest's size). Every track named Captions or Captions N holding only text clips is looked at: a track whose pages are all in one caption style Frame Job makes (Highlight, Pill, Karaoke, Build or One Word, with its slide, fill and dim looks; recognised by the page's font and word_style) is re-paged from the words its pages hold — every hand correction kept — by the same pager that made them, each page staying inside its clip, then put back at the same place in the stack with the same name, hidden and locked as before. A track is kept as placed, and listed with its reason, when it is a matte track, holds a page with no word timings (Subtitles pages included), holds a page none of whose words starts inside it, holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make, has pages in more than one style, or would not fit (the clip ceiling). One undo step "Re-lay Captions". Refused with nothing to re-lay: "relay_captions found no caption track it can re-lay: " and each kept track with its reason. Answers {ok, relaid [{track (the new track), replaced (the old one), name, style, pages}], kept [{track, name, reason}], project}.

content.content:
So "split this clip at the playhead" or "make the selected titles bigger" mean what you'd expect. The block isn't updated during the assistant's turn. After its own edits, the assistant reads the project again.

## The transcript

The transcript is one block of text. You can select across entries and copy it as plain text. It scrolls to the newest line as the reply arrives.

| What you see | Style |
|---|---|
| Your message | Semibold |
| The assistant's reply, streamed as it is written | Regular |
| Its working notes between tool calls | Small, faint |
| One line per tool call: the tool's name and its arguments, e.g. `split (at: 96000, clips: [12])` (first 70 characters) | Small monospace |
| `failed: …` for a tool call that was refused, with the reason | Small monospace |
| `Allowed: …` / `Declined: …` for each permission question, or `Declined (stop): …`, `Declined (close): …` or `Declined (helper): …` when it was declined by Stop, by closing the window or by the helper stopping | Small monospace |
| Compaction and clearing notes, and notes about key, model or spend-ledger problems | Small monospace |
| `Cost: …` at the end of each turn | Small monospace |
| Errors | Red |

Errors you may see:

- "API error *status*: *message*": Anthropic refused or failed the request (a bad key, a rate limit, an outage). Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before this appears. A bad key fails at once.
- "The reply was cut off at the output limit."
- "The model declined this request."
- "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."

If the helper stops, a waiting question is declined. Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. Click **Clear** to start clean.

If a response's cost cannot be written to the spend ledger, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.

The assistant works for up to 30 rounds of tool calls in one turn, then stops.

**Clear** (↺) ends the conversation, empties the transcript and resets the Spend row and the meter. The meter keeps the model's window size, so it reads "0 of *L* tokens · 0%" until the next response. Your next message starts a fresh conversation. Closing the window also ends its conversation. Conversations aren't saved with the project, and each window has its own.

## What the assistant can do

The assistant has the same tools an agent has over MCP (see [MCP](mcp.md)), with a few exceptions listed below. It can:

- open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest
- add, remove, reorder and set tracks; add and edit markers; change the canvas
- import, relink and remove media, copy it into the project (it asks first), and set a media's camera log
- place media, text, shapes, backgrounds, adjustment clips and graphics; insert, overwrite, paste and duplicate
- move, trim, split, slip, roll, rate-stretch, ripple-delete, lift, insert time and close gaps; detach audio and attach it again, and make J- and L-cuts
- nest clips, or take a nest apart
- set speed, reverse, freeze frames and add speed ramps (see [Speed](speed.md))
- change how a clip looks and sounds, including transitions, actions and zooms; rename a clip, hide or mute it, and paste attributes
- import captions, transcribe on this Mac, read a clip's timed words, and export captions
- find silences and filler words, normalize loudness and synchronize audio
- write, place and change graphics modules; import fonts and assets; rename, delete or restore a module
- export, check an export's progress, or cancel it
- render a frame of the timeline to look at the result, before and after a visual edit

Every edit is one undo step on the project, the same as your own. A turn isn't grouped: each edit is its own step, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten Undos, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names each step after its edit, as it does for an agent's call over MCP. **Edit ▸ Undo** (⌘Z) outside the message field takes back the assistant's last change. You can also ask the assistant to undo.

**How it behaves.** Its replies are short, a sentence or two, and don't repeat what the tool lines already show. It writes or restyles captions only when you ask. It renders a frame to look before and after a visual edit. The model runs at medium effort with thinking on, and the faint working notes between tool calls are its thinking updates.

The assistant works only on its own window's project. A tool call that names another project is refused.

**Cutting words.** Ask it to take out filler words and it finds them and cuts them in one step, but only in media that already have a cloud transcript made with filler words (by **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**). The assistant can't upload audio to make one, so in other media it cuts nothing (the search reports which media have no such transcript). Ask it to remove a false start and it reads the clip's words and their times (from the media's cached transcript, or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, never the network), says which words it will cut, then cuts them as one undo step. It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what was a false start is a judgement call. See [Clean-up tools](cleanup-tools.md).

### Tools it will not call
| Tool | The question reads |
|---|---|
| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*" (or REPLACES) |
| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*" (or REPLACES); "save_project writes a file" when no path is known |
| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |
| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", `.framejob` added when missing (only with a `path`) |

A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.

Other tools the assistant can call write files without asking: `render_frame` writes a PNG (to a temporary file, or to a path the model names), and `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font` and `import_graphic_asset` write graphics modules, fonts and assets into the project's package.

While a question waits, the **Assistant** tab title shows a small dot, whichever inspector tab you are on. Answer with a click: Return never answers a question. Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. **Deny** tells the assistant you declined, and it won't retry that call in the same turn unless you ask. Stopping the turn, closing the window or the helper stopping each count as a decline. Other windows' assistants and agents over MCP keep working while one window waits for an answer.

### While you are dragging

If one of the assistant's tool calls arrives while you are in the middle of a drag (on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider), it waits until you release the mouse. Then it runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the assistant's change or mixes with it. The same applies to agents over MCP.

The assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.

### Stopping a turn

Click **Stop** (the Send button while a turn runs). Stop:

- ends the request to Anthropic
- declines a question that is waiting
- answers every tool call that has not started yet with "Cancelled by the user."
- cancels an on-device transcription or transcript read that is running. Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.

An export is handed to the Export Queue as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the assistant to cancel it. See [Export](export.md).

## Long conversations: the context meter and compaction

The **Context** meter shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response:

- "Nothing reported yet" before the first response
- "*N* of *L* tokens · *P*%" once the model's window is known (shortened to "*N* / *L* · *P*%" or "*P*%" when the inspector is narrow; the tooltip always has the full figure)
- "*N* tokens (window size unknown)" if Anthropic did not report the window size

The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns red past 80%.

**Compaction.** With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is summarised at the end of the first turn that passes the threshold, never in the middle of a turn. The summary keeps what you asked for and your stated preferences, the project and the clips, tracks, markers and media involved, the edits made and undone, and what is still open. The transcript notes "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" and then "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.". If no summary comes back, the note says compaction didn't finish and that it will try again after the next turn. The summary request is priced like any other response.

With compaction off, a conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click **Clear**.

**Clearing old tool results.** With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It keeps the five most recent, clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time, and can happen mid-turn. Each clearing adds a note, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view.", and costs a fresh prompt-cache write. The model may have to fetch something again after a clearing.

## What it costs

Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. All the figures below are **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.

### Per turn

Each turn ends with a line in the transcript:

`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`

The part in brackets names the price table and its date: "bundled table of …" (the copy built into the app), "cached …" or "fetched …" (a copy Frame Job refreshes at most once a day). If a refresh failed, the line adds "not refreshed:" and the reason.

- A response that could not be priced shows as "unknown (*reason*)", never $0, followed by "at least" the part that could be priced.
- A response cut short by Stop or an error is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
- Amounts are shown to four decimal places. A tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001".

### Per conversation

The tab's **Spend** row adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation:

- "Nothing yet" before the first response
- "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate"
- "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" when a response was cut short or could not be priced (shortened to "≥$…" when narrow)
- "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" for a tiny positive amount (shortened to "<$0.0001" when narrow)
- "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" when nothing could be priced

Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

### Per month

Under the buttons in **Settings ▸ Assistant**, a line totals the current calendar month in UTC, for example "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses.". Variants report "Nothing recorded in …", responses that could not be priced, and ledger lines that could not be read. Totals are rounded to the cent, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.01". While the ledger is being read the line says "Reading the spend ledger…", and if it cannot be read, "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*.". The line refreshes when Settings opens and after each response while Settings is visible. Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

The figures come from a spend ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, with one line per response: the time, the model, the token counts and the dollars. It never records your key or the conversation's content.

## Privacy: what leaves your Mac

When you use the assistant, these go to Anthropic, under your key:
